classification_reasons: Spec is tight (every flagged concern closed by the panel or the owner, acceptance measurable), but the blast radius is wide: 9 app modules rewritten or deleted, the public frame contract loses three columns, BinanceBanError, the um market and the 1s interval, and the cache moves to a new subtree.
The paging and completeness logic (rest.py, loader.py) is new code, covered only by new tests against a new stub; the old suite does not cover it.
No risk-list item is touched (gate risk-hits: none), and there is no schema migration of stored data.
attempted: Intent: the diff replaces Binance with KuCoin REST only (SPOT_URL and FUTURES_URL in rest.py), deletes vision.py and the thread pool, keeps the public names, drops BinanceBanError, keeps 0.1.0, maps markets spot/futures, intervals with 6h refused on futures and 1s refused, eight columns, close_time = open + interval - 1, quote_volume from turnover, and puts the futures-volume note in the load_klines docstring and the download epilog. Every intent bullet matched; nothing nearby-but-different.

Spec and plan: R1-R29 checked against the code. Every file in the diff stat is in plan.md 'Files that change' (the change-folder files hook-log.jsonl, run-build.json, verifier.md and status.yaml are process records). The build departures (test split into test_data.py, test_data_rest.py and test_data_cache.py plus conftest.py, _open_ms, an empty-after-grid REST day settled as MISSING, one extra help test) are written into plan.md Risks in the same diff.

Spot paging, backwards: window_end starts at end_ms. Each page is filtered to [start, window_end) and window_end = min(open), so it strictly decreases and the loop is bounded. An empty page sets covered to the whole range, which is correct because each request spans [start, window_end) whole, so a quiet stretch cannot end the range early (R21). A failure gives covered = [window_end, end), which is right because KuCoin keeps the newest rows, so every candle in [oldest, previous end) was returned.

Futures paging, forwards: to = end - 1 on every page (the verifier's first URL confirms it). Rows are filtered to [window_start, end), which drops the end-of-window row, and window_start = max(open) + interval, so it strictly increases. A failure gives covered = [start, window_start), which is right because KuCoin keeps the oldest rows. The current day's in-progress candle is dropped by _expected_ms/_on_grid, and today is never cached.

DownloadError part way: _page catches it, fetch_range returns the coverage so far with error set, _rest_pass settles every day of the range (complete closed days are cached), then raises. Later ranges are not fetched. sync_days does not return, so the CLI gets the error and exits 2. Tests check spot (the later day 10-01 cached) and futures (failing on call 9, 09-29 cached).

Completeness: REST only when the day lies wholly inside the covered span and has rows. A partly covered day is MISSING with the failure as reason, gaps are found per grid time, and it is not cached. A day with no rows gets NO_CANDLES, BEFORE_FIRST or NO_CANDLES_ON_DAY as R20 says. _worth_caching is source == REST, and a closed REST day with rows only off the grid becomes MISSING, so an empty day is never cached.

Untrusted input: the body bound runs before the parse. JSON ValueError and RecursionError are caught. A non-dict envelope, a code that is not 200000 or a status that is not 200 is a refusal. msg and code are cut to length and stripped of non-printable characters (isprintable also strips the Cf bidi controls). Rows must be lists of exactly 7 items: strings on spot, non-bool numbers on futures. Times must be whole numbers inside 64 bits including open + interval - 1. Prices go through _finite (nan, inf and 1e400 rejected). OverflowError is caught on futures. URLs are built with urlencode from validated symbols and fixed hosts. Path escape is refused by the symbol regex (no '.' or '/') and by day_path's is_relative_to.

Observation, not a park: in both directions a page that has rows, all of them outside the asked window, is filtered to empty and ends paging as fully covered. spec Design said such a page is an unexpected response. plan step 4 orders the filter first, which makes that guard unreachable, as the verifier noted. This only happens if KuCoin returns rows outside the window it was asked for, which contradicts the measured behaviour. The worst case would be a short day cached as complete. Worth a one-line hardening later; it breaks nothing under the measured API.

Proof: no build.log, test.log or lint.log is committed. This is a runner-deferred session (SDLC_GATE_COMMANDS=runner), and verifier.md says the targets are the runner's. Not treated as missing proof. verifier.md exercised the changed behaviour through the stub: multi-page loads, the end-of-window row, gaps, refusals, DownloadError on each market, the CLI, the pacer, retries and redirects. Its observed values agree with the test assertions (2820/4120 gap counts, cached file names, sleeps [20.0, 60.0]).

Tests could pass with a bug present? The stub enforces the measured rules (spot end exclusive and newest kept, futures to inclusive and oldest kept, page caps 1500/200). The tests pin call counts, the first URLs, exact Gap tuples and the cached file lists, so a wrong window rule or wrong coverage would fail them. One weak spot: test_futures_end_of_window_row_adds_no_next_day_candle would also pass without rest.py's '< end_ms' filter, because the loader's per-day filter and _on_grid drop the row too. The outcome is still guaranteed, by two layers.

Pre-existing tests: this is a feature-type change. The deleted Binance tests and fixtures are declared in plan.md Proof with the ratchet line, as the intent allows. Every Proof test name exists: I grepped tests/ and found 44 names plus test_help_notes_short_days_and_lost_futures_days. Behaviours that stay keep equivalent tests: retries, redirect with a KuCoin origin, https only, datetime bounds, cache root, atomic write, cache-info/clear with binance-vision untouched.
Skip markers: none added (no skip or xfail anywhere under tests/).

Blast radius: callers of load_klines (frame shape, markets, short frames), cache_info/clear_cache (new subtree), and scripts/measure_storage.py (eight columns, validate_symbol(symbol, market)) are all updated. No other importer of app.data. No guardrail file in the diff (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml and policies/** untouched). CLAUDE.md is now outdated on lines 5-6, 30 and 36-37, and plan.md names those lines for the owner's own PR, as REVIEW.md requires. No new dependency, so pyproject.toml and ci.yml are unchanged.

Policies: security-baseline rule 2 is applied as above. Rule 3: no key or secret. Rule 7: the tests are offline (stub and sequence fetches only). data-conventions: the schema is defined once in schema.py, and the deprecation note is in the load_klines and __init__ docstrings (panel #1). ux-and-brand: one-line errors, exit 2, copy in module constants (SOURCE_LABELS, DOWNLOAD_NOTES, CLEAR_NOTE). coding-standards: type hints, frozen dataclasses, dead Vision code removed. No policies/<name>.md beyond README and no project skill override exists.

Claims against today's code: read_day's schema check (an old-schema file is refetched), the cache_root priority, the atomic write, the 0002 opener without a redirect handler, and parse_date's datetime refusal all survive unchanged. Rate limits: RATE_LIMIT_RESERVE 100 and MAX_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT 60 are as decided by panel #2. A 429 with only gw-ratelimit-reset waits at most 60 s, never above MAX_RETRY_AFTER, so it never stops early. 418 is now returned like any 4xx.
Drive: sdlc.yaml commands.drive not consulted; the plan lists no drive files and the change has no evidence/proof/ directory, so angle 9 does not apply.
Risk list: gate risk-hits reported none; no brief written.
